sources.summary: From a puffer made of old fishing nets to a trench worthy of Bogart, these are the coats worth braving the cold for • The best men’s shirts for every occasion No one remembers the suit Humphrey Bogart wore at the end of Casablanca, but everyone remembers the trench. The same goes for you this winter: from November to March, your coat is your first impression, so it’s worth getting right. That doesn’t mean you have to spend a fortune: the coats in this list cost £200 or less. The trick to choosing the best coat for you is buying something you’ll still be happy to wear in five years. If you’re feeling unsure, stick to timeless colours – navy, black, camel, brown or moody greens – and shapes that have been around forever: the overcoat, the trench, the car coat or, a more recent classic, the puffer. sources.name: The Guardian
sources.summary: The legendary country singer says he did everything wrong. Yet now, at 93, he’s music’s last man standing. What’s the secret of his longevity? • Read an exclusive extract from Willie Nelson’s memoir here Before the interview, Willie Nelson’s publicist warns me that there’s only one thing the 93-year-old country music legend doesn’t like to discuss: the past. Which rules out talking about the 150-plus albums he’s made; the Highwaymen, the supergroup he formed with Kris Kristofferson, Johnny Cash and Waylon Jennings; writing On the Road Again on an aeroplane sick bag. It also rules out talking about paying off a $32m tax bill with a double album called The IRS Tapes; co-founding Farm Aid with Neil Young and John Mellencamp; taking $40,000 off Woody Harrelson in a single poker session; or breaking up a massive brawl in a parking lot with two Colt 45s before signing autographs for cops. No, the publicist says, it’s all about the future for Willie. And what does that primarily consist of, I ask. Gigging and his cannabis business, Willie’s Reserve, she explains. After an extensive vetting process, the publicist tells me my chat with Willie will be one of my life’s highlights. We normally ask a minimum of an hour for an interview. The publicist offers 10 minutes. We eventually negotiate an extra five minutes. Fifteen minutes with Willie will do me. Continue reading...
